AWARD 1. IO filed 'Detailed Accident Report' (DAR) with respect to the accident before this tribunal on 29.03.2022.
Copy of DAR was supplied to all the parties.

2. Brief facts of the case are that on 21.06.2021, petitioner was going to park near Azadpur Metro Station, Delhi along with her aunt Savitri and Om, who is son of Savitri and when they were crossing the service road near Azadpur Metro Station, in the meantime a battery e-rickshaw, being driven by its driver / respondent no.1 at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner came from Model Town side and suddenly applied brake due to which it turned turtle on the road and caused injuries to petitioner Baby Divyanshi on her hand and head.
Petitioner was initially taken to Vinayak Hospital, Delhi and from there to Civil Line Hospital from where she was referred to Lok Nayak Hospital where she was treated vide MLC no. 22140/21.

3. Respondents no. 1 & 2 (driver & owner of the offending vehicle) through have filed their separate written statements but taken similar pleas that their vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and respondent no. 1 and vehicle of respondent no. 2 have been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is further stated that their vehicle Baby Divyanshi Vs. Rajat Kumar & Ors.
MACT no. 149/22 Page 5 was duly insured with respondent no. 3/ Ins. Co.

However, in its written statement, it has taken the plea that respondent no. 1 was holding learner's driving licence and a person holding learner's driving licence cannot drive the vehicle in public place.
Hence respondent no. 3 / Ins. /Co. denied its liability.
It further denied its liability on other technical grounds as well.

PW3 has not at all been cross examined by respondents no. 1 and 2 particularly by respondent no. 1 nor respondent no. 1 has examined himself to prove that he was not rash and negligent or that he has been falsely implicated in the present case or that accident had occurred due to negligence of petitioner.
Further, criminal case record filed on record shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/338 IPC.

Apart from deposition of PWs, the fact that petitioner suffered injuries in the accident is also supported by her medical documents Ex.PW1/B (colly) and Ex. PW1/B duly proved by PW1 Sh. Anil Kumar Record clerk.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
There is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his implication in the present case.

Further, relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under: -

Being injured, petitioner Baby Divyanshi is well within her rights to claim compensation from the respondents.
Now coming to the quantum of compensation.

13. It is deposed by father / natural guardian of petitioner as PW2 that from the spot, petitioner was initially taken to Vinayak Hospital, Delhi and from there to Civil Line Hospital from where she was refereed to Lok Nayak Hospital where she was treated vide MLC no. 22140/21.
Due to this accident he suffered 2-3 months income loss i.e. about 50,000/- and incurred about Rs. 1 lac on the medical treatment, conveyance, special diet etc. and claimed Rs. 10 lacs compensation.

Admittedly,
petitioner got treatment from Government Hospital and no medical bills have been placed on record.
Accordingly, no amount is awarded to the petitioner towards medical expenses.
14. There is no evidence except deposition of PW2 Dharamveer to verify that any amount has been spent on special diet, conveyance or attendant etc.

However, seeing nature of injuries suffered by petitioner, a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards special diet, Rs.10,000/- for conveyance and Rs. 5000/-
towards attendant charges awarded to the petitioner.
Though, it is stated that by father / natural guardian of petitioner as PW2 that he suffered 2-3 months income loss i.e. about 50,000/-, however no evidence has been brought in this regard.

However, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner and hospitalization as well as follow up treatement, it is presumed that father /
natural guardian of petitioner could not continue his work for one month.
Hence, an amount of Rs.15,908/-, as per minimum wages of unskilled worker, towards loss of income during the treatment is also awarded to the petitioner.

Now coming to the aspect of liability.
16. It is already held above that accident has been caused due to rash and negligent driving by the respondent no. 1 and admittedly, the offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co.

However, it was the contention of respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. that respondent no. 1 was not having Divyanshi vs Rajat Kumar on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148477357/

valid driving licence, as he was holding learner's driving licence and respondent no. 1 was driving without letter 'L' affixed on the vehicle and was on public road without any instructor and

to prove the same, respondent no. 3 examined R3W1 Paramvir Singh, Senior Executive Legal, who relied upon the documents i.e. copy of insurance policy Ex. R3W1/B and learner driving licence of respondent no. 1 as Ex. R3W1/2.
Perusal of Ex. R3W1/2 i.e. learner licence of respondent no. 1 shows that it was valid from 30.12.2020 to 29.06.2021.

As respondent no. 1 had not led any evidence to prove that he was having valid driving licence at the time of accident or that he was driving on public road along with instructor along with letter 'L' affixed on the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Neither respondent no. 1 examined himself nor produced any valid driving licence, which interalia proves that respondent no. 1 was not having any valid driving licence at the time of accident.

Since, the respondent no. 1 / driver has failed to produce any valid driving license,
an adverse inference is drawn against him.

Hence, respondent no. 3 / insurance company has been able to establish its statutory defence, as respondent no. 1 has failed to produce his valid driving licence, which amounts to breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

But, being the insurer, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. is primarily liable to indemnify the insured under section 149 (1)
of the MV Act.

Since Baby Divyanshi Vs. Rajat Kumar & Ors.

Perusal of Ex. R3W1/2 i.e. learner licence of respondent no. 1 shows that it was valid from 30.12.2020 to 29.06.2021.
As respondent no. 1 had not led any evidence to prove that he was having valid driving licence at the time of accident or that he was driving on public road along with instructor along with letter 'L' affixed on the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Neither respondent no. 1 examined himself nor produced any valid driving licence, which interalia proves that respondent no. 1 was not having any valid driving licence at the time of accident.
Since, the respondent no. 1 / driver has failed to produce any valid driving license,
an adverse inference is drawn against him.
Hence, respondent no. 3 / insurance company has been able to establish its statutory defence, as respondent no. 1 has failed to produce his valid driving licence, which amounts to breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
But, being the insurer, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. is primarily liable to indemnify the insured under section 149 (1)
of the MV Act.
Since Baby Divyanshi Vs. Rajat Kumar & Ors.
MACT no. 149/22 Page 10 respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has been able to establish its statutory defence, so respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. is at a liberty to recover the compensation amount from the respondents no. 1 and 2 (driver and owner of offending vehicle) jointly and severally but after paying the compensation amount to the petitioner.
